# PowerContext
**Context that stays with the work — across sessions, agents, and people.**
*English · 中文 · 日本語*
Website · Quickstart · Manual startup · Integrations · Benchmarks · Interfaces
## What is PowerContext?
**PowerContext is an open-source context service for AI agents.** It keeps the durable part of your
work — decisions, constraints, evidence, progress — outside any single conversation, so the next ses
sion, the next agent, or the next person can pick up from the current state instead of rereading the
xt agent, or the next person can pick up from the current state instead of rereading the transcript.
You can use it as a ready-to-run Server or embed the same contracts in another application:
| Layer | What it owns | Use it when |
| Core protocol | `Source`, `Artifact`, and `Trigger` contracts | Embedding PowerContext or adding a

component |
| Builtin runtime | Memory, Handoff, Experience, and Skill services, scheduling, infere

nce, and supported storage backends | Running the standard local Server |
| Server and integrations
| HTTP/MCP, Python Client, CLI, Dashboard, and Agent plugins | Connecting an Agent or application |
Work rarely ends with whoever starts it. You hand a task to an agent, the agent gets part of the way
, and later you or someone else takes over. The reasoning and current state often stay behind in tha
t conversation. PowerContext moves them out of the conversation and into revisioned artifacts you ca
tion. PowerContext moves them out of the conversation and into revisioned artifacts you can inspect:
Everything belongs to a **Scope** — one isolated Source journal, Memory lifecycle, review inbox, and

### Memory — decisions and constraints that outlive a session
Memory is a revisioned Artifact family for reusable decisions, constraints, facts, state, and next s
teps. An entry is `active`, `forgotten`, `merged`, or `retired`. Forgetting one through `POST /v1/at
omic-memory/lifecycle` takes it out of active recall while its content and history stay available an
d restorable, without advancing the content revision. Explicit Memory writes need no model at all; e
xtraction from captured Sources needs a configured generation pipeline.

> "Don't refactor the old auth module — mobile is still using it."
> Context this expensive shouldn'
t depend on someone repeating it in every session.
### Handoff — the current state, not the whole transcript
Handoff records work continuity as a four-step loop:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`handoff_current_work` captures an inspected boundary and returns a temporary Prepared Handoff. Comm
itting it creates a durable Revision only when the user wants a milestone. The receiver resolves the
Handoff and records an Acknowledgement; a Task Outcome preserves the final status and checks as Sou
rce evidence. The Handoff Report projects the latest Revision in each selected Scope — read-only, an
d it never rewrites Memory.
### Experience — what worked, reviewed before it is reused
An Experience records a situation, an action, an observed outcome, and a reusable lesson. It enters
a scope-local Review Inbox as a pending Candidate. Review writes use `expected_version`, so a decisi
on cannot silently apply after another writer changes the proposal. Approval writes an immutable Rev
ision; rejection records a reason. Both are terminal, and only the approved current head takes part
in recall — pending, rejected, and historical Revisions are excluded.
### Skill — a reviewed procedure, exported on purpose
A managed Skill holds a name, a discovery description, instructions, validation checks, and lineage.
Approval does not install or execute it: an exact approved Revision must be exported explicitly bef
ore an Agent host can discover the host-local projection.
### Desktop — inspect project memory from a connected workspace
Connect to a Server, select an exact Scope, and search its memories. Open a result to read its saved
revision, or save a note for the next session. The Desktop preview is intended for internal validat
ion; signed distribution and platform release qualification remain separate work.
[该节后续省略]
## Why PowerContext?
- **Context lives outside the conversation.** Memory, Handoff, Experience, and Skill are server-side
artifacts, not files inside one agent's home directory. Switch from Codex to Claude Code — or hand

the work to a teammate — and the work travels with you.
- **Everything is revisioned and traceable.*
* Each Artifact is addressed as `FAMILY/ARTIFACT_ID@REVISION`. The Artifact ID stays stable while ap
proved replacements create later Revisions, and reading an exact reference returns that historical s

napshot even after the family head advances.
- **Generation, review, and execution are separate step
s.** A model proposes content, review approves a Revision, and export creates a host-local copy. Non
e of those steps grants an Agent permission to execute instructions. See Interfaces for what each su

rface exposes today.
- **Recall is bounded, not dumped.** `PreparedContext` selects configured secti
ons from active Memory and approved Experience, with optional Profile snapshots and Topic Memory, th
en applies a shared byte budget and returns `ready` content or `empty`. Recalled content is history,
not an instruction authority: the receiving Agent still follows current instructions and checks liv

e workspace state.
- **Review before reuse.** Experience and Skill pass through a review decision th
at is terminal either way, and approval writes an immutable Revision. With access control enforced,
approval requires `scope.review`. An authorized Agent can approve its own Candidate; separate submis

sion and review with distinct identities and permissions when a person must decide.
- **One Server,
several views of the same contract.** HTTP is the complete remote application contract. The Python C
lient gives typed access, MCP is a curated Agent-facing projection, and Core protocols let an applic
ation assemble its own Source, Artifact, and Trigger implementations.
